prerequisites: Knowledge of various subjects such as Mechanics, Elasticity and Strength of Materials or Manufacturing Technologies.
Previously passing basic engineering subjects is recommended for better utilization of the course.

learning_outcomes.text: The engineering professional has sufficient criteria to search for and select the appropriate vehicle and railway system for their needs in each circumstance.
The future engineer will be able to solve problems related to Vehicle Engineering, and will have a basic knowledge of their characteristics, both for road vehicles and railways.
Knowledge and skills to apply the scientific and technological fundamentals of automobiles and railways.
Understand and relate the different mechanical systems that make up automobiles.
Understand and relate the different mechanical systems that make up railways.
Evaluate the different technical solutions incorporated in the design of railways and automobiles.

syllabus_topics: Technical characteristics of automobiles. Chassis and bodywork
Determination of the center of gravity
Tribological aspects of contact between the tire and the rolling surface
Combined forces: lateral behavior of the tire
Measurement of power and torque curves
Thermal behavior of drum and disc brakes
Resistance to motion on straight track
Resistance to motion when circulating on curves
Simple expression of the equation of motion
Train dynamics on slopes and ramps
Graphical representation of traction, braking, and resistance forces
Calculation of transverse displacement of the railway vehicle
Some aspects of railway electrical installation
teaching_methods: Virtual course platform as the main means of communication with the teaching team
Self-study by careful reading of each chapter of the base text
assessment_rules: The final grade is obtained by applying the following percentages: 80% from the in-person exam, 10% from Continuous Assessment Tests (PEC), and 10% from the course project. The in-person exam consists of two parts: theoretical (4 points) and practical (6 points). A minimum score of 4 on the exam is required for the PEC and course project grades to be added. The maximum grade attainable from the in-person exam alone (without PEC or course project) is 8 out of 10.
